data.title: Web App Manifest
data.tagline: A JSON file that describes a Web app's name, icons, and launch behavior
data.learningOutcome: You can trace the installed name, icon, launch URL, and window mode back to Manifest fields and distinguish install configuration from offline capability.
data.description: A page links to this JSON file with a manifest link, and a browser can use its name, icons, start_url, and display to create an install entry and launch window. Having a Manifest does not by itself provide complete offline PWA behavior.

learning.assumes: You have seen a browser offer an install entry for a site or opened a manifest.json file.
learning.outcome: You can trace the installed name, icon, launch URL, and window mode back to Manifest fields and distinguish install configuration from offline capability.

distinctions.label: Favicon
distinctions.explanation: Web App Manifest supplies app name, icon, and launch information for an install entry; a Favicon supplies the site icon for browser tabs, bookmarks, and history.

distinctions.label: App Icon
distinctions.explanation: The Web App Manifest icons field points to artwork usable by installation; App Icon is the visual object as it appears in operating-system surfaces.

explanation.title: It describes identity and launch behavior
explanation.text: name affects the installed name, icons provide system artwork, start_url sets the launch address, and display influences whether it opens like an app or a normal tab. The page must link the intended file.

explanation.title: The installed result is the evidence
explanation.text: After editing the file, reinstall and check the name, icon, launch path, and window mode. A page opening in a browser proves only that it is reachable, not that install metadata is correct.

data.boundary: Web App Manifest describes Web app installation and launch information; a Favicon mainly serves browser tabs and bookmarks; offline caching needs other runtime mechanisms. A Manifest alone does not guarantee offline support.

lessonPractice.title: An installed site always opens at the wrong path. What should you check first?

options.label: Check the Manifest start_url and verify the launch address after reinstalling
options.feedback: Correct. The default installed launch address comes from install configuration such as the Manifest, not from changing the Favicon.

options.label: Change the Favicon because the browser infers the launch path from it
options.feedback: A Favicon identifies a site in browser surfaces; it does not define the installed default URL.

options.label: Only add a Service Worker and assume the launch address will become correct
options.feedback: A Service Worker relates to caching or offline behavior and cannot replace checking the Manifest start_url.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the Web App Manifest referenced by manifest link and check name, icons, start_url, and display. After fixing it, remove and reinstall the app, then verify the Home Screen name, icon, launch URL, and window mode. Do not equate installability with offline support.
